name: MCE Sandbox
summary: A sandbox comparing prime-sieve implementations across Perl with MCE and Inline::C, C with OpenMP, and Codon. Seven .codon files carry the sieve variants, and they are the reason Codon is present: primes2 reimplements the reference algorithm, primes4 drives the libprimesieve C API, and the cpusieve, gpusieve and pgpusieve trio walk the same range sieve from CPU parallelism up to Codon's @par(gpu=True) form. Second GPU-annotated Codon code found in the index.
why_codon: README names Codon as one of the three implementation technologies under comparison and labels each Codon variant by what it exercises, including the @par(gpu=True) syntax.

name: Benchmarking Mojo
summary: A cross-language benchmark suite written for a 2024 Bachelor's thesis on Mojo, run from a Docker image over softmax, quicksort, matmul and crc16. Codon is one of the languages measured rather than the subject: five .codon files hold the four algorithms plus a shared bench_suite harness.
why_codon: README frames the repo as benchmarking Mojo; Codon appears as one of the compared languages. No Codon-specific claim is made.
note: Bachelor's thesis work rather than a taught-course exercise; filed as coursework because no separate thesis value exists in the vocabulary.

name: Awesome Mojo
summary: A curated list of Mojo code and problem solutions that carries a small cross-language benchmark set alongside it. Codon appears there as a comparison language: three .codon files cover recursive and iterative Fibonacci and the multibrot set, each timed with hyperfine against the equivalents in other languages.
why_codon: README gives the hyperfine invocations that time codon run --release against the other languages in the same benchmark.

name: hello-pythran
summary: A small comparison of Python acceleration approaches organised as parallel source trees, one per technology. Codon holds two of them: a Fibonacci implementation and a pattern-match example, twenty lines in total, sitting beside the Pythran equivalents.
why_codon: Repo makes no written claim. Inferred from the src/main/codon and src/main/codon_one trees sitting alongside the Pythran trees that Codon is one of the accelerators being compared.

name: markhend/aoc
summary: Advent of Code solutions kept across many languages, one directory per year and day. Codon is one of the languages exercised: seven .codon files spread over the 2020 and 2021 puzzles, each a standalone solution using no Codon-specific feature.
why_codon: No claim and no comparison prose. Inferred from the polyglot layout that Codon is being tried as one solution language among many.

name: takechi-scratch/atcoder
summary: Competitive programming solutions for AtCoder contests. Codon enters through the site's May 2025 language test, where four .codon files solve the standard practice problems, with one further solution filed under a recent contest round.
why_codon: No written claim. Inferred from the language-test-202505 directory that Codon is being trialled as an AtCoder submission language.

name: tsp-solver
summary: Metaheuristics for the travelling salesman problem, the main line of work written in Python across several local-search variants. A single .codon file ports the naive local-search solver; no other variant has a Codon counterpart.
why_codon: README documents the Python variants only and never mentions Codon. Inferred from the single .codon port of tsp_ls_naive that Codon was tried on one solver; no timing or comparison is published in the repo.
note: Filed exploration rather than benchmark: a Python counterpart exists, but the repo publishes no comparison.
